title: Cycle 21: Budget / Quota-Aware Adaptive Warmup Gating
weak_spots: HTTP 402 Insufficient Balance was mapped to .unknown and did not trip the circuit breaker as an economic failure
Rate-limit / quota response headers were ignored by health probes
Adaptive warmup scoring used reliability x latency only, so a fast but depleted provider could win
No per-(provider, baseURL) quota snapshot store existed
ModelsTabView did not surface economic signals to the user
Circuit breaker .balance and .auth failures used the same cooldown as transient errors
files_changed: rings/SR-00/ModelHealthService.swift — ProviderQuotaStatus enum, ModelHealthResult.quota, header parsing, 402 mapping
rings/SR-00/ModelWarmupService.swift — quota multiplier scoring, strictQuotaGating parameter
rings/SR-00/ModelConfigurationStore.swift — quota service injection, strict gating toggle, status helper
BR-OUTPUT/ModelsTabView.swift — strict quota gating toggle, quota badges in adaptive warmup section

next_options.name: Predictive background warmup scheduling
next_options.summary: Run adaptive warmup proactively every 30-60s and cache the winning endpoint so send path never pays the probe cost.

next_options.name: User-defined provider preference order
next_options.summary: Allow drag-to-rank providers in ModelsTabView and blend explicit priority into warmup scoring.

next_options.name: Real-time spend dashboard
next_options.summary: Capture usage headers from responses, estimate per-provider spend, and show a running balance/cost badge.

notes: Strict quota gating toggle is off by default so existing behavior is preserved; when enabled, depleted endpoints are excluded from warmup selection unless they are the current selection.
Quotas are tracked per endpoint, not per model, because provider-wide balance/rate-limit signals apply to the whole base URL.
Unit tests were added but could not be executed in the current toolchain because XCTest is unavailable; they will run when Xcode is installed.
